I found the Vandermonde results. They support a stationary picture in rescaled zero coordinates, provided we keep the force from the zeros outside the selected group. I’m using that framework to compare the late-time zeros with an equally spaced lattice and to bound the errors in both its density and its Vandermonde determinant.

The stationary-state idea now gives two useful formulas: a Gaussian profile at negative time, and an equally spaced zero pattern after rescaling at positive time. I also found a necessary distinction: convergence at every fixed height does not imply uniform convergence over all heights. With the regulator fixed, the density vanishes at sufficiently large height for each finite time. I’m making that distinction explicit in the error bounds.

The bounds now give a concrete version of your proposal. At negative time, the Gaussian density approximation has an absolute error of order \(|t|^{-3}\), uniformly across all real heights. At positive time, I have a growing-window estimate for the averaged clock profile and its Vandermonde determinant. I’m checking the constants and recording where the simple positive-time formula stops being uniform.

The Vandermonde calculation strengthens the result: it gives a determinant error bound for a growing block of zeros, beyond the earlier fixed-label asymptotics. The bound tends to zero, although its conservative finite-time values are still loose for the largest blocks. I’m saving the proofs, numerical checks, limitations, and updated progress ledger now.

The stationary-state idea works **after rescaling**, and the Vandermonde framework gives a quantitative version.

For \(t=-T\to-\infty\), use
\[
G_T(z)=\frac{\Phi(0)\sqrt\pi}{2\sqrt T}e^{-z^2/(4T)}
\]
in the original density formula. I derived an explicit **absolute error \(O(T^{-3})\)**, uniformly over every real height \(x\), with \(|y|\le A\sqrt T\). Consequently, \(T^2\rho_\epsilon(-T,\sqrt T\,z)\) approaches a fixed profile with error \(O(T^{-1})\). Details are in [Note 11](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics/notes/11_TWO_TIME_LIMITS_ALL_HEIGHT_ERROR_20261024.md).

For \(t\to+\infty\), the averaged density satisfies
\[
R(t,x,y)=\frac{L(t)}{\pi}k_h(y)
+O\!\left(\kappa^{-1/2}+L^{-3}\right),
\]
where
\[
4\pi e^{4L}=2tL+9,\qquad \kappa=8tL-2t+36.
\]
This holds on growing height windows \(X\asymp\kappa^{1/3}\), with the averaging support inside them. Thus \(\pi R/L\) becomes stationary; the physical intensity grows like \(\log t/(4\pi)\).

For consecutive blocks of zeros within those windows, I also obtained
\[
\Delta_m(t)=
\left(\frac{\pi}{L(t)}\right)^{m(m-1)}
\prod_{k=1}^{m-1}(k!)^2\,e^{o(1)},
\]
with an explicit error bound permitting a growing number of zeros. The corresponding rescaled Vandermonde Hessian approaches that of equally spaced points. See [Note 12](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics/notes/12_GROWING_HEIGHT_STATIONARY_CLOCK_AND_VANDERMONDE_20261024.md).

One limitation matters: with fixed \(\epsilon\), this positive-time clock cannot converge uniformly over **all** heights simultaneously. I proved that obstruction and supplied a separate, computationally expensive analytic expansion with an all-height truncation bound.
